A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Infini-gram mini research and contain complete main text and Appendices A–K. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of equations, tables, figures, and screenshots; all appendix pages render identically.

before.justification: v3 reports original indexing-time, memory-use, and query-latency measurements, plus benchmark-contamination analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original systems measurements and benchmark-contamination results, including the detailed appendix tables and case studies.

M1.justification: The UTF-8 byte FM-index, parallel construction, sampled suffix and inverse suffix arrays, and disk-backed querying procedures remain unchanged in Sections 2–3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions index the Pile, DCLM-baseline, and the same seven January–July 2025 Common Crawl snapshots. Contamination analysis retains the same 24 benchmarks across five task groups.

E2.justification: SDSL remains the construction-time and memory comparator in Section 3.1, and infini-gram (Liu et al., 2024) remains the latency comparator in Appendix D, Table 5. The added citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Query-testing settings, hardware, benchmark sampling, and contamination thresholds are unchanged. Both retain 50-character substrings with a one-word stride and downsampling large benchmark test sets to 1,000 entries.

E4.justification: The indexing-step breakdown, query-length and reconstruction-length analyses, dirty-entry categorization, and seven contamination case studies are retained unchanged in Section 4.3 and Appendices B–D and H–I.

E5.justification: Both retain averaging over 100 random queries per setting in Appendix C. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Indexing costs and latency results in Tables 1 and 3–5, contamination rates and counts in Tables 2 and 7, and qualitative contamination findings are unchanged. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: FM-index definitions, LF mapping, complexity reasoning, and querying mathematics in Section 2 and Appendix A are unchanged. Section 4.1 also retains the same contamination-score definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about compressed scalable search, construction efficiency, indexing 83 TB, and large-scale benchmark-contamination monitoring. Citation repairs do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of contamination and possible evaluation inflation. Limitations concerning retrieval latency, multi-pattern searches, case-sensitive exact matching, and problematic retrieved content are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, sampling parameters, hardware specifications, preprocessing, judge model and prompt, corpus licenses, and code/API/data access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new reproducibility details.

R1.justification: v5 replaces unresolved citations with Guo (2025), Depuydt et al. (2023), Bevilacqua et al. (2022), and Sainz et al. (2024), adding their bibliography entries. It removes Simpson and Durbin (2010). These are limited attribution changes; the research-positioning narrative remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 repairs citation text, adds National AI Research Lab Project funding to the acknowledgments, and updates the arXiv version/date header. Scientific prose and section/appendix organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Longer citations and the funding acknowledgment produce small column-break, page-break, spacing, and bibliography-layout shifts. Figures and tables retain their designs and content; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v3 contains unresolved citations for prior FM-index applications and shared contamination reporting; v5 identifies these sources and supplies bibliography entries. This improves attribution and traceability, while leaving the methods, empirical evidence, conclusions, and limitations unchanged.
